title: Angle Pairs: Complementary, Supplementary, and Vertical Angles
seo_title: Angle Pairs Worksheet: Complementary, Supplementary, Vertical Angles (Geometry) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Prove theorems about lines and angles. Theorems include: vertical angles are congruent; when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are congruent; points on a perpendicular bisector of a line segment are exactly those equidistant from the segment's endpoints.
meta_desc: Free Geometry worksheet on angle pairs: the Angle Addition Postulate, bisectors, complementary and supplementary angles, vertical angles and linear pairs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Complementary angles add to 90°. Supplementary angles add to 180°.
key_sub: Vertical angles are congruent. A linear pair adds to 180°.
body_html:
How it works

Angle Addition Postulate: if D is inside ∠ABC, then m∠ABD + m∠DBC = m∠ABC. An angle bisector splits an angle into two congruent angles.

  • Complementary angles add to 90°. Supplementary angles add to 180°.
  • A linear pair is two adjacent angles on a straight line. They are supplementary.
  • Vertical angles are across from each other where two lines cross. They are congruent.
Example

Two angles form a linear pair. One is (3x + 20)° and the other is (2x + 10)°. Find both angles.

A linear pair adds to 180: 5x + 30 = 180

x = 30

3(30) + 20 = 110 and 2(30) + 10 = 70

Answer: 110° and 70°

Example

An angle is 10° more than its complement. Find the angle.

Complement = x, angle = x + 10

x + x + 10 = 90, so x = 40

Answer: 50°

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up the totals. Complementary is 90° (C comes before S, 90 before 180).
  • Setting a linear pair equal. Linear pairs add to 180°; only vertical angles are equal.
  • Stopping at x when the question asks for an angle measure.
  • Thinking any two angles that add to 180° form a linear pair. They must also be adjacent.

faq.q: What is the difference between complementary and supplementary angles?
faq.a: Complementary angles add to 90 degrees. Supplementary angles add to 180 degrees.
Yes. When two lines intersect, the angles across from each other always have equal measures.
Two adjacent angles whose outer sides form a straight line. A linear pair always adds to 180 degrees.

faq.q: What is the Angle Addition Postulate?
faq.a: If a point D is in the interior of angle ABC, then the measure of angle ABD plus the measure of angle DBC equals the measure of angle ABC.

items.q: Two angles are supplementary, and their measures are in the ratio 4 : 5. Find the measure of the larger angle.
items.e: Supplementary angles add to 180°. Split 180° into 9 parts: 180 ÷ 9 = 20° per part. Larger angle = 5 × 20° = 100°.

items.e: The angle between the handles is across from the angle between the blades. Vertical angles are congruent: 49°.

items.q: A wheelchair ramp makes a 21° angle with the flat ground. What angle does the ramp make with the ground on its other side, along the same straight line?
items.e: The two angles form a linear pair along the ground, so they add to 180°: 180° − 21° = 159°.

Two angles are complementary, and their measures are in the ratio 1 : 4. Find the measure of the larger angle.
items.e: Complementary angles add to 90°. Split 90° into 5 parts: 90 ÷ 5 = 18° per part. Larger angle = 4 × 18° = 72°.

items.q: Two angles are complementary, and their measures are in the ratio 1 : 5. Find the measure of the larger angle.

items.q: Is this statement always, sometimes, or never true? A linear pair of angles is complementary.
items.e: A linear pair adds to 180°, not 90°. It is supplementary. Never true.

items.q: Is this statement always, sometimes, or never true? Two supplementary angles form a linear pair.
items.e: They also need to be adjacent (side by side). Two separate angles can add to 180°. Sometimes true.

items.q: Two angles are supplementary, and their measures are in the ratio 1 : 2. Find the measure of the larger angle.
items.e: Supplementary angles add to 180°. Split 180° into 3 parts: 180 ÷ 3 = 60° per part. Larger angle = 2 × 60° = 120°.

items.q: A wheelchair ramp makes a 8° angle with the flat ground. What angle does the ramp make with the ground on its other side, along the same straight line?
items.e: The two angles form a linear pair along the ground, so they add to 180°: 180° − 8° = 172°.

items.q: Is this statement always, sometimes, or never true? An obtuse angle has a complement.
items.e: An obtuse angle is more than 90°, so nothing positive adds to it to make 90°. Never true.
